text.p: Philips, the Dutch electronics firm and one of the largest airfreight shippers in Europe, is inviting airlines to meetings to discuss their "unprofessional" conduct concerning the implementation of fuel surcharges.
Kees van der Vleuten, air transport manager of Philips, said there had been no negotiation with the manufacturer or explanation concerning the level of surcharges.
"We do not know how exactly they have been calculated. But the amount of carriers introducing the charges at the same level could suggest some 'conspiracy'", he said.

Another problem, he added, has been the timing of the surcharges. Philips had just finished their bi-annual rates negotiations with the carriers and distributed contracts within Philips. Then two weeks later the surcharges started to be introduced, he added.

"We have had no time to prepare ourselves. We can't charge this on to our customers." But currently, the carriers have enough cargo, it is a sellers market but he added: "It will be interesting to see what happens in January."

He questioned the airline's vulnerability to changes in fuel prices. "Because airlines have such short-term contracts, if there is a change in the fuel prices their back is against the wall. This is not flexible enough."
The industry needs a professional rates adjustment structure to cope with these increases.

"Philips has mixed feelings about it, we don't want to say we don't want to pay it but we are against these charges." It is virtually impossible to refuse to pay this, he said. "We are confronted with this issue from the Netherlands to Singapore."
But he stressed: "We would like more explanation as to how these charges are formulated and a chance to negotiate."
